description: Na₂LiCl₃ is Caswellsilverite-like structured and crystallizes in the tetragonal I4/mmm space group. Na is bonded to six Cl atoms to form NaCl₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one LiCl₆ octahedra, corners with five equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, edges with four equivalent LiCl₆ octahedra, and edges with eight equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-4°. There are a spread of Na-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.69-2.82 Å. Li is bonded to six Cl atoms to form LiCl₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent LiCl₆ octahedra, edges with four equivalent LiCl₆ octahedra, and edges with eight equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are two shorter (2.60 Å) and four longer (2.74 Å) Li-Cl bond lengths. There are three inequivalent Cl sites. In the first Cl site, Cl is bonded to five equivalent Na and one Li atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ClNa₅Li octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-4°. In the second Cl site, Cl is bonded to two equivalent Na and four equivalent Li atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ClNa₂Li₄ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. Both Cl-Na bond lengths are 2.69 Å. In the third Cl site, Cl is bonded to two equivalent Na and four equivalent Li atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ClNa₂Li₄ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. All Cl-Li bond lengths are 2.74 Å.
